assignment.rule: Identified customers with at least one recorded order in the window.

incremental.label: estimated incremental effect (treatment vs holdout)
incremental.primary_metric: orders per assigned customer over the campaign window
reasons: small_sample: fewer than 30 measured customers in an arm; the interval is unreliable, so no conclusion is drawn

measured_profit.label: measured incremental profit (from simulated outcomes)
measured_profit.formula: ΔP = Î×(AOV−VC) − R×d − C  (≡ Î×(AOV−d−VC) − (R−Î)×d − C)

caveats: Outcomes are simulated from synthetic data and assumed parameters; they are not observations of real customers and do not show real merchant uplift.
The simulated true effect was taken from this version's own expected scenario, so agreement with the prediction is by construction: this tests the measurement pipeline, not the prediction.
Welch's t interval is approximate for skewed order counts; it is reasonable with at least 30 measured customers per group, and verdicts are withheld below that.
One pre-specified primary metric (orders per customer) is tested once; profit is derived from it. Repeated looks or extra metrics would need a multiple-comparison correction.
Order value and variable cost are the merchant-entered settings used by the prediction; per-order values are not simulated.
The profit interval reflects uncertainty in incremental orders only; redemptions are treated as fixed.
Some outcomes are missing; they are assumed missing at random and estimates are scaled to all treated customers.
notice: SIMULATED execution on synthetic data. No offer was sent and no real customer, merchant or payment system was contacted. Simulated results do not show that a real campaign would work.
